entities.summary:
Li Dian, courtesy name Mancheng, was a Chinese military general and politician serving under the warlord Cao Cao during the late Eastern Han dynasty of China. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Guandu in 200, where Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao, securing his position as a key ally. Li Dian also participated in the Battle of Xiaoyao Ford in 214–215, where he led the defense of Hefei against the forces of Sun Quan.

 As a significant figure in Cao Cao's regime, Li Dian contributed to the military campaigns and strategic decisions that shaped the Eastern Han dynasty. His involvement in these battles demonstrates his importance as a military leader and politician in this period of Chinese history.

 The legacy of Li Dian can be seen in the continued influence of Cao Cao's regime on Chinese politics and military strategy during the late Eastern Han dynasty. His actions and decisions had a lasting impact on the development of Chinese military tactics and the balance of power in the region.

 One notable aspect of Li Dian's legacy is the enduring importance of the Battle of Xiaoyao Ford, which remains a significant event in Chinese history and a testament to the military prowess of the Eastern Han dynasty.
